main_text.p: stituit Deus & præcepit volūtate sua ineluc-ta-bili,sit futurum irritum.Efaiæ 14. Nam(vt ait Efaias) Ie-houa exercituum iniuit consiliū,& quis irritum faciat? & manum eius extentam quis auertat? Quòd si in hac misera constitutione nostra æquè in nobis ac in aliis fratribus nostris & seruis Domini nostri Iefu Christi interdū quàm plu-rima animadvertimus abesse longissimè ab illa ratione quam salutari consilio suo constituit Deus; immò etiā nonnullos qui ex cösilio̸[?] eius ad hanc, communione pertinent, indignissimè hanc ipsam communionē dissuere, & atrocissimè per-rumpere: tamen non ad præsens illorū factum, sed ad æternum Dei consilij atq. mandatū gra-tiæ referre animos nostros oportet constantissi-mè;vt tū ipsi de nobis infirmissimis vasis spem concipiamus in Domino, tum etiā de aliis me-liora speremus omnia: in quibus superciliosè damnandis atq. expungendis partim facto ip-sorum, partimq. studiis & infirmitatibus plus æquo operam (proh dolor) confumimus.

Itaq. si hic hominem male agentem video, illic tamen Deum bene ordinantem contemplor in eadem communione sanctorum, & illa ipsa mala quæ ab homine sunt plenitudine infinitæ gratiæ obtegentem, vt extincto peccato seruetur homo ad vitam in die illo obtinendam. Atq. hic demùm circumfulget nos illa infinitas gratiæ & beneficentiæ diuinæ, cùm in homine misero & peccatis dante operā miserrimè animaduerto simul, tum fidem decreti illius & consilij æterni, quod Deus

page.notes: Left margin: one bare reference "Efaiæ 14." placed beside line 2. The word "cösilio" in the line "ex cösilio eius ad hanc" is doubtful and is marked [?]; the first letter may be "c" with a mark over it. The paragraph break before "Itaq." is inferred from a short line ending. The spaced running head is printed "EI R E N I C I" and is given here as EIRENICI. Small stray marks at the foot under "Deus" are not printed text and are omitted. The line-end hyphens are as printed.
